data.narrative:
SemiQon is a Series A quantum computing company that has raised €19.5M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a sector comp universe of 11 peers: 3 public companies (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private firms including Quantinuum, IonQ, D-Wave Quantum, Rigetti Computing, and Infleqtion.

The peer-median method proved inapplicable in this case. Despite identifying 5 same-sector peers in quantum computing, the dataset contains zero companies at the same stage, zero at adjacent stages, and zero within a similar valuation tier. The threshold for statistical reliability requires a minimum of 3 comparable datapoints across these filters; the absence of meaningful overlap prevents use of this triangulation approach. Falling back to an all-sector median would introduce substantial distortion given the early-stage capital requirements and technical risk profile specific to quantum hardware development.

Without sufficient narrow peer clustering to support quantitative triangulation, the analysis cannot produce a defensible valuation range. The key uncertainty is the extreme heterogeneity in the quantum computing sector—peers range across different technology platforms (trapped ion, superconducting, neutral atom, annealing), commercial maturity stages, and capital structures. A credible valuation would require either (1) expansion of the dataset to capture additional Series A quantum firms, or (2) a shift in methodology toward founder background, IP strength, and funding velocity as supplementary anchors.
